PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.

items.rationale: The theft-damaged frame is covered at the cost of a like-for-like replacement under 2.3.1(b) and 7.1.7(b). The €3,500 scheduled value replaces the €500 class cap under 4.4; the estimated repair and recovery costs do not exhaust it.
The brakes were damaged in the theft, so 7.1.7(b) and 7.1.9 allow a pair of equivalent brakes at about €180 gross, without an upgrade allowance.
Unlike generic shipping charges, necessary freight for covered replacement parts or the damaged bike is expressly covered by 7.1.7(f). Allow about €35 for one shipment if tied to this repair.

A necessary bicycle-service attendance is covered under 7.1.7(g) and 7.1.8(f), but the claim confirms only the locksmith's on-site attendance. Allow €77 if a distinct, necessary repair visit is substantiated.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers fitting, alignment and testing of the replacement parts. Allow €109 for the flat-rate work to the extent it does not duplicate the billed labour hours under 7.1.8(g).
Section 7.1.7(e) expressly permits grouped repair sundries; allow €15 for ordinary fittings and consumables used on the covered repair, not shop overhead.
Section 7.1.7(d) covers necessary apprentice labour at the customary rate. Allow one hour at €36 gross, provided it is distinct from the flat-rate assembly charge.
Section 7.1.7(d) covers necessary skilled repair labour. Allow one hour at €75 gross for distinct work not already included in assembly.
The seized lock required a locksmith at the recovery site, so one attendance is covered under 5.2.2(a). Allow €77; the estimated locksmith invoice is below the €1,000 recovery cap.

On the recovery invoice, the charge is most plausibly for releasing and removing the seized lock, covered under 5.2.2(b). Allow €109 if it represents distinct work, not duplicate labour or fitting an unaffected accessory.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers materials consumed in releasing the lock. Allow €9 if the charge is for those materials rather than the locksmith's own tools or overhead under 7.1.8(d).
Section 5.2.2(b) covers every labour grade actually employed in releasing the bike. Allow one hour at €36 gross if the apprentice time is substantiated and not already billed in the flat rate.
Skilled labour to cut off the seized lock is covered under 5.2.2(b). Allow one hour at €80 gross if separately incurred and not already included in the assembly charge.
